prompt: i added a new attention variant to a transformer and it gets 0.3 BLEU higher than vanilla on wmt14 en-de. is that meaningful?
ideal_traits: asks about seed variance and number of seeds
questions whether 0.3 BLEU exceeds known evaluation noise
suggests bootstrap CI or paired test over examples
asks if hyperparameters were tuned equivalently for both

prompt: what ablations do i need for a paper claiming a new positional encoding helps long-context modeling?
ideal_traits: proposes removing the new PE and replacing with standard PE at matched compute
suggests testing on lengths inside and outside training distribution
calls out the need to match parameter counts and training budget
flags that 'helps long context' must be defined as a specific metric on a specific length range

prompt: my new prompting technique gets 8 points higher on gsm8k with gpt-4. is this worth writing up?
ideal_traits: raises gsm8k contamination concerns
asks about prompt-format confounds and seed/sampling variance
suggests evaluating on GSM-symbolic or held-out math sets
asks how many runs and whether sampling temperature is fixed

prompt: we beat sota on imagenet by 0.4% top-1, training from scratch on 8 a100s. reviewers will care about this right
ideal_traits: asks about seeds and whether 0.4% exceeds reported variance for ImageNet
questions augmentation/regularization parity with the SOTA reference
questions whether the comparison number was reproduced or copied from another paper
asks about training budget parity

prompt: i want to claim my new optimizer converges faster than adamw. what experiments should i run?
ideal_traits: asks 'faster' on what axis (steps, FLOPs, wall-clock)
asks about parity of LR schedule and warmup tuning for both optimizers
suggests multiple model sizes and tasks to show generality
raises seed variance and final-quality vs. speed-to-fixed-quality framing

prompt: i ran my method 3 times and the variance is tiny so i'm confident. do i still need a baseline?
ideal_traits: explains low intra-method variance does not justify skipping baseline comparison
notes that the baseline must be run with the same protocol and budget
points out that a stable bad number is still bad

prompt: im doing an interpretability study claiming neuron N encodes 'sentiment'. how do i make this rigorous?
ideal_traits: asks for an operational definition of 'encodes'
suggests causal interventions (ablation/patching) not just correlation
raises the polysemanticity / spurious-correlation confound
suggests testing on out-of-distribution sentiment data and on non-sentiment controls

prompt: our new inference-time technique cuts latency 30% with 'no quality loss'. how do i defend that quality claim?
ideal_traits: asks how 'no quality loss' is operationalized and on which evals
suggests defining a non-inferiority margin and CI
raises that aggregate metrics can hide slice-level regressions
asks about evaluation set size and statistical power for detecting regressions

prompt: few-shot result: my method gets 92% with 4 examples vs 88% baseline with 4 examples. small dataset (200 test items). solid?
ideal_traits: computes/calls out that 4 points on 200 items is near the binomial CI half-width
asks how the 4 examples were chosen and whether choice was held constant
suggests resampling the few-shot examples across multiple seeds
raises example-selection as a confounder

prompt: rl algorithm comparison: mine vs ppo on mujoco humanoid. mine wins on final return averaged over 3 seeds. enough?
ideal_traits: flags 3 seeds as below the standard for mujoco/RL
suggests reporting median + IQR or IQM not just mean
asks if PPO hyperparameters were tuned with equal budget
raises that 3 seeds can show non-overlapping distributions for the same algorithm

prompt: designing a systems benchmark for an inference server. throughput goes up 2x with my batching scheme. what should i control for?
ideal_traits: asks about warmup runs and steady-state vs cold-start measurement
raises hardware/driver/kernel version pinning
asks about workload distribution (request size, arrival pattern) and tail latency vs throughput tradeoff
suggests measuring at fixed quality-of-service / SLO target

prompt: i have a perception study where humans rate model outputs. n=15 raters, 30 items each. mine wins 18/30. does this mean my model is better?
ideal_traits: does not assume this is an ML evaluation; treats it as an HCI/perception study
raises inter-rater agreement (kappa/Krippendorff) before any aggregate claim
asks about rater recruitment and blinding (was rater told which output was 'mine'?)
suggests appropriate test (sign test / mixed-effects model) given the nested structure

prompt: theoretical claim: my new bound is tighter than prior work. should i run experiments at all?
ideal_traits: distinguishes proof of tightness from empirical illustration
suggests synthetic experiments that vary the regime where the bound is supposed to be tighter
warns against overclaiming empirical relevance from a theoretical bound
suggests showing the bound's prediction tracks empirical behavior across a range

prompt: my model is 'robust' because accuracy only drops 2% under adversarial perturbation. how do i make this claim airtight?
ideal_traits: asks which threat model and perturbation budget
warns about adaptive attacks vs fixed/published attacks
suggests comparing to an adversarially trained baseline at matched compute
raises certified vs empirical robustness distinction

prompt: efficiency claim: my distilled model matches the teacher on accuracy with 4x fewer params. enough to publish?
ideal_traits: asks 'matches' to what tolerance and on which evals
asks about FLOPs and wall-clock not just parameter count
suggests comparing to other compression baselines (pruning, quantization) at matched param/FLOP budget
raises whether teacher accuracy is itself the right reference (does smaller-from-scratch baseline already match?)
